selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how different kinds of people benefit from the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It says people at every level, from the least educated to the most learned, receive guidance from it and can gain from its teachings.

questions.question: Which groups of scholars are especially mentioned as drawing knowledge from the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Experts in Islamic law, many Islamic fields of study, and scholars of belief and religious foundations are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by calling the Qur'an a source of truth and a mine of reality?
questions.answer: It means the Qur'an contains deep and reliable knowledge that scholars can keep drawing from.

questions.question: Why is the failure of non-Muslim Arab literary experts important in this passage?
questions.answer: Because they were highly skilled in language and strongly motivated to challenge the Qur'an, yet they still could not produce anything equal to it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about matching even a single sura?
questions.answer: It says people were unable to produce something equal even to one sura.

questions.question: According to the passage, is eloquence the only miraculous feature of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: No. Eloquence is presented as only one part of its miraculous nature.

questions.question: What does the continued inability of later speakers and scholars show?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur'an’s miraculous quality is not limited to one time period and remains beyond human power.

questions.question: What is one sign in the passage that the Qur'an is meant for all people, not just a small group?
questions.answer: The passage says every class of people can receive a share from its teaching and understand even deep truths from it.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Qur'an to many fields of Islamic knowledge?
questions.answer: It says scholars in many disciplines find their needed principles and answers in the Qur'an.

questions.question: Why does this support the idea that the Qur'an is true?
questions.answer: Because one book giving guidance to many levels of people and many sciences suggests great depth and reliability.

questions.question: Why were Arab masters of language in a strong position to challenge the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They were highly advanced in literature and had reason to oppose it, so they had both the skill and motive to try.

questions.question: What happened when they tried to oppose it?
questions.answer: They could not produce something equal to it, even at the level of one sura or one aspect of its miraculousness.

questions.question: What does the silence of later famous speakers and scholars mean in the passage?
questions.answer: It means they were unable to answer the Qur'an’s challenge despite wanting fame through opposition.

questions.question: What does human inability to match any aspect of the Qur'an lead the passage to conclude?
questions.answer: It leads to the conclusion that the Qur'an is a miracle beyond human power.

questions.question: In the passage, what shows that the Qur'an teaches both ordinary people and experts?
questions.answer: It benefits all levels of humanity, while also providing deep truths for highly trained scholars.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the depth of the Qur'an by saying many sciences draw from it?
questions.answer: It implies that the Qur'an has layers of meaning rich enough to support many branches of knowledge.

questions.question: How is the phrase about a mine of reality different from saying the Qur'an is just useful?
questions.answer: It means the Qur'an is not only helpful but full of lasting truths that can be continuously discovered.

questions.question: Who are the two broad groups mentioned in the challenge to the Qur'an’s literary power?
questions.answer: First, early non-Muslim Arab literary experts, and second, later famous speakers and scholars who wanted to oppose it.

questions.question: What is important about the fact that even one sura could not be matched?
questions.answer: It shows that the challenge is so great that even the smallest unit mentioned remained beyond human ability.

questions.question: Why does the passage say eloquence alone is not the whole issue?
questions.answer: Because the Qur'an’s miraculousness includes other major aspects besides beautiful language.

questions.question: How does the passage extend this argument beyond the early Arabs?
questions.answer: It says later eloquent speakers and scholars also failed when trying to challenge the Qur'an.

questions.question: What broad claim does the passage make about who can understand the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It claims that people across the full range of human ability can benefit from it and grasp its teachings according to their level.

questions.question: How do scholars serve as evidence in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: Their ability to derive principles and answers for many fields from the Qur'an is presented as proof of its truth and depth.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the Qur'an’s relationship to knowledge?
questions.answer: It shows the Qur'an as a foundation that nourishes many kinds of religious learning.
